title: WASM extension authoring: Rust for devs, simple language for game designers
description:
Define the supported languages for writing Tier 2 WASM game extensions. Two tiers of authoring:

**Rust (power users):** Same toolchain as engine. GameExtension trait, compile to wasm32-wasi, smallest binaries. Template project with cargo-generate. For programmers contributing complex game logic (mental poker, Go scoring, chain reactions).

**Simple language (game designers):** Need a pure, expression-oriented language that compiles to WASM. Candidates: AssemblyScript (TS-like, npm toolchain), a Lisp-like DSL (s-expressions, pure functions, no mutation — fits the declarative philosophy), or a purpose-built functional DSL. Requirements: no side effects, no mutation, no loops (recursion with fuel instead), JSON-in/JSON-out interface, small binaries, easy to learn for non-programmers who understand game rules but not systems programming. The language should feel like writing game rules, not writing code.

Deliverables: (1) Decide on the simple language. (2) Extension interface spec (WIT or exported functions). (3) Rust template project. (4) Simple-language template project. (5) Documentation for both paths.
